translationRepairs: At first Cang's father Chang was not full five chi tall; Cang was more than eight chi tall; Cang's son again was eight chi tall; reaching the grandson Lei was more than six chi tall.
At first, Cang's father was not a full five chi tall; Cang was over eight chi tall; Cang's son was likewise eight chi tall; his grandson Lei was over six chi tall.
Parallel 蒼長八尺餘, 蒼子復長八尺, and 孫類長六尺餘 shows that 長 means stature, not a father named Chang; the revised literal also removes the proposal's awkward bracketed pronoun.
Cang came; Marquis of Jiang and others honored and established Emperor Xiaowen; in the fourth year he replaced Guan Ying as chancellor.
Zhang Cang and the Marquis of Jiang and the others honored and installed the King of Dai as Emperor Xiaowen; in the fourth year, Cang replaced Guan Ying as chancellor.
Wikisource and ctext preserve 蒼與絳侯等尊立代王為孝文皇帝: Cang jointly enthroned the King of Dai. The local 來 and omission of 代王為 are source defects, not wording to retain.
